lead.headline: Binance says $6.3bn was stolen in what may be the biggest hack ever, and analysts blame North Korea
lead.short: Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday that $6.3bn of digital assets had been hit in what could be the largest hack in history. About half has been frozen, but much remains with the hackers, and Binance says it will cover all losses. Early checks suggest an engineer's compromised laptop allowed unauthorised withdrawals.

why.text: Western agencies say North Korea uses stolen crypto to pay for its nuclear and missile programmes, and millions of Indians trade on exchanges like Binance.

more: The analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis both attributed the theft to a North Korean unit called TraderTraitor; Chainalysis said it had "high confidence". TRM's Ari Redbord called it a "watershed moment" and said efforts to trace and recover the funds were far from over. The previous record was $1.5bn stolen from the Bybit exchange in 2025.

Binance did not respond directly to questions about North Korea, saying it was "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals". Withdrawals are disabled, co-chief executive Yi He said, thanking token issuers for freezing assets. Binance.US, a separate platform for American customers, says it is not affected.

facts.suspect: North Korea's TraderTraitor unit (TRM Labs, Chainalysis)

seconds.headline: Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats and Arab parties a record 19, and Likud claims the election was 'stolen'
seconds.short: Israel's count is complete: Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's 48, both short of 61. The two Arab-led lists won a record 19, making them potential kingmakers. Likud alleged voters had been "bribed" to back Arab parties, after the elections committee asked the Shin Bet to investigate claims of Qatari funding.

why.text: Netanyahu's camp is trying to rule out the only coalition that could replace him, while he pushes for renewed war with Iran.

more: Qatar denied the claims as "ridiculous and dangerous". The Shin Bet said its inquiry did not implicate a whole community that had voted legally, and the elections committee's acting director, Dean Livne, said there was "no basis for allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity". Eisenkot and Arab leaders accused Netanyahu of trying to delegitimise the vote.

Both main blocs had ruled out governing with the Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, but the left-wing leader Yair Golan has urged a government "in partnership" with them. The results go to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday, and he will then choose who gets the first chance to form a government.

update.new: Final count: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot 48, Arab parties 19; Likud alleges fraud.
update.front: The count is final, and Netanyahu's party is now calling the result stolen.

seconds.headline: Four days before the midterms, Democrats lead by about 8 points and Trump cancels two weekend rallies
seconds.short: With four days to go before the 3 November midterms, Democrats lead Republicans by 51.4% to 43.2% in the RealClearPolling average, a gap of about 8 points. Donald Trump has cancelled rallies in Kansas and Iowa and will campaign by telephone in nearly 20 states. A Marquette poll in Wisconsin put his approval at 37% and disapproval at 61%.

why.text: A Democratic Congress would check Trump's war plans for Iran, which his aides say could follow the vote.

more: Only 16% of Wisconsin voters said they were better off than a year ago. "Democrats are more enthusiastic and more certain they will vote," said Charles Franklin, director of the Marquette poll, though he warned that polls are not perfect predictions and close races could go either way.

In Texas, the Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 49% to 43% in a CNN poll, and in Michigan Abdul El-Sayed leads Mike Rogers 49% to 42%. In Alaska, a legal dispute over two candidates who share the name Dan Sullivan could keep the Senate result in court after polls close.

update.new: Democrats lead by 8 points; Trump cancels rallies.
update.front: The last weekend before the vote, with Democrats ahead and Trump off the road.

seconds.headline: A glacial lake bursts in Bhutan, and more than 4,500 people are moved from the Sankosh riverbank in Bengal
seconds.short: A glacial lake, Shintaphu in Bhutan's Gasa district, burst on Thursday, sending floodwater down the Sankosh river towards India. West Bengal moved more than 4,500 people living by the river into about 10 relief camps, and parts of Assam were put on alert. By morning the water had passed Alipurduar well below the danger level.

why.text: Glacial lake bursts are becoming more common as the Himalayas warm, and India's northern rivers carry the water.

more: The floodwater reached Alipurduar at about 3am. "The water level in River Sankosh is much below the danger level," chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said, adding that 47 people first reported missing were safe and officials had worked through the night. Shintaphu is considered one of Bhutan's potentially dangerous glacial lakes.

The Jal Shakti ministry warned Alipurduar in Bengal and Dhubri in Assam that water could rise suddenly and reach the border in six to eight hours. Bhutan's broadcaster said people there had been told to move to safer places. The scale of the outburst was not immediately known, and officials in Bengal said they had been well prepared.

seconds.headline: Rahul Gandhi opposes the sale of IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax, as the finance ministry says its reserve price was never changed
seconds.short: Rahul Gandhi wrote to IDBI Bank's employees that "public banks are not assets to be sold off, they are tools to build the nation", questioning the sale to Fairfax, a Canadian firm. The government and LIC own 95% of the bank and will keep 34% after the sale. The finance ministry defended its valuation process.

why.text: It is the biggest bank privatisation in decades, and its terms will shape any future sale of a state-owned lender.

more: "Seven years ago, IDBI was losing money. Last year, it earned a profit of over nine thousand crore rupees. That turnaround is your work," Gandhi wrote in the letter dated 29 October. He said the government had promised Parliament in 2003 that it would always hold at least 50% of IDBI.

He also warned that reservation for SC, ST and OBC candidates would end once the bank is private. The finance ministry says the reserve price for the sale was not changed during the process. IDBI began as a pioneering development bank before becoming a commercial lender, and Gandhi said its employees had carried it through that change.

briefs.headline: More than 55,000 people are evacuated across nine Odisha districts, and 10,000 shelter in camps in Andhra's Ichchapuram
briefs.text: More than 55,000 people have been evacuated in Odisha, and 10,000 are in camps after the Bahuda river flooded Ichchapuram in Srikakulam, where NH-16 is still under water and power is out. Crops on 21,519 hectares are damaged, initial estimates show, and the water is receding fast, the collector said.

update.new: Evacuations pass 55,000; Andhra floods after the Bahuda swells.

stories.headline: US intelligence believes Nvidia's Jensen Huang was targeted by an alleged Chinese spy who did business with him
stories.byline: THE GUARDIAN · NEW YORK TIMES · 30 OCT
stories.short: US intelligence agencies believe Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore data-centre company Megaspeed, the New York Times reports. Officials had watched her on suspicion of smuggling Nvidia chips to China and concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset passing commercial information to Beijing. The two are not related.

why.text: Nvidia's chips are the heart of the AI race, and the chip export rules affect what India can buy too.

more: White House officials are reportedly alarmed because of Jensen Huang's close relationship with Donald Trump. The administration has restricted exports of advanced AI chips to China on national security grounds, and Megaspeed was suspected of helping get around those rules.

"Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year," Nvidia said, adding that Megaspeed and similar customers "receive ordinary business information, not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets, and zero information relevant to national security". Megaspeed's Alice Huang is of no relation to the Nvidia chief. In Mumbai, IT shares rose 2.4% to a three-month high at 2pm.

briefs.headline: The rupee heads for its best month since February, helped by RBI steps that keep oil companies' dollar demand off the market
briefs.text: It was at 95.25 a dollar at 11:30 on Friday, up about 0.6% in October. Traders say the RBI's interventions have been smaller lately; reserves are down about $65bn from August's record.

update.new: October is shaping up as the rupee's best month since February.

stories.headline: Chinese versions of FC Online and eFootball drop Mbappé, as state media call Madrid's apology late and superficial
stories.short: The fallout from Kylian Mbappé's Mao remark has spread to video games: the Chinese versions of FC Online and Konami's eFootball titles are removing promotional material featuring him. Chinese state-linked outlets have criticised Real Madrid's apology as late, and a provincial propaganda department called the response superficial. Madrid visit Racing Santander on Sunday.

why.text: The row keeps growing, and Madrid's biggest commercial market in Asia is now asking for more than words.

more: The Global Times had contrasted the club's handling of Mbappé's comments with its public stance on the racist abuse of Vinícius. Mbappé apologised on 27 October and Madrid on 28 October; China Media Group still has La Liga off air, and three Chinese brands have ended their deals with the striker.

On the pitch, Arda Güler and Fede Valverde followed individual programmes in training. Carlo Ancelotti named Vinícius Júnior and Endrick in his Brazil squad but left out Éder Militão. France's football federation president has backed Mbappé after his apology. Madrid are third in La Liga, three points behind Barcelona, after the Clásico win.

facts.games: FC Online and eFootball, Chinese versions

update.new: The games pull Mbappé content; state media criticise Madrid.

stories.headline: Djokovic loses to Struff for the first time in nine meetings, and drops out of the top 10 in the race to the ATP Finals
stories.short: Novak Djokovic lost 6-7, 7-5, 7-6 to Jan-Lennard Struff in the second round in Basel, his first defeat in nine meetings with the German, ranked 27th. The result dents his hopes of a record 19th ATP Finals. He is now outside the top 10 of the race to Turin for the first time since 2018.

why.text: At 39, Djokovic may miss the season finale he has won a record seven times.

more: "The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance," Struff said. Djokovic is 319 points behind Rafael Jodar, who holds the last qualifying place, and can still move up at the Paris Masters in November.

The ATP Finals run from 15 to 22 November; Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton are confirmed, and Jannik Sinner is out injured. Shelton, the top seed in Basel, also lost, to the Swiss wild card Jerome Kym, ranked 222nd. Djokovic last failed to qualify on merit in 2017, and he has missed the past two editions with injury.

update.new: Djokovic lost to Struff in round two.

briefs.headline: Robin Uthappa joins Mumbai Indians as batting coach as the five-time champions overhaul their staff before IPL 2027
briefs.text: The five-time champions are rebuilding for 2027. Mitchell McClenaghan becomes bowling coach, while Lasith Malinga and Paras Mhambrey leave. Uthappa, a 2007 World T20 winner, played 86 games for Kolkata Knight Riders.
